idiom_name: ConcurrentDictionary.TryAdd plus a transactional inbox / framework deduplication
implementation_notes: In-process, ConcurrentDictionary<TKey,TValue>.TryAdd is the atomic claim: it returns false when another thread already claimed the key, so it replaces the contains-then-add pair. For durability, let the business write itself be the claim - a unique index on the idempotency key, catching the resulting DbUpdateException - or keep an inbox table written inside the same DbContext transaction. The dominant frameworks ship the whole pattern: NServiceBus implements built-in message deduplication in its outbox, and MassTransit's consumer outbox tracks received message ids for exactly-once consumer behaviour; prefer those over hand-rolling the store when the stack is already there.
pitfalls: TryAdd on a process-local dictionary gives no protection across scaled-out instances or restarts; pair it with a durable claim when duplicates can outlive the process.
The unique-constraint violation is the durable claim, so catch DbUpdateException narrowly around the inbox insert - a broad catch around the handler hides real failures.
Inbox row and business rows must share one DbContext transaction, otherwise a crash between the two reopens the duplicate window.
